necessity_assessment.conclusion: Recording the distinction is necessary, but narrowly: only k's verdict change is attributable solely to it. The package overstates breadth (claims k, s, h) and uses a strawman filter test, while omitting the decisive argument.
necessity_assessment.decisive_argument_missing_from_package: Both v1 k-pairs (REGISTER R-90 vs REGISTER-rule; OPEN-WORK note vs OPEN-WORK ruling) are identical on every v1 field except k itself and outcome, so no analysis-time filter over v1 fields can separate them without filtering on the variable under test.
overstatement: s: v1 support is circular by construction (D9) regardless of the norm/act split; an anti-circularity rule removes it without r2
h: the only v1 pair has an UNCLEAR side with no source text; it fails on anchoring under v1 already
necessity_assessment.filter_strawman: Package tests single fields and 'drop START'. The combined filter r=EXECUTION AND genre=register-row removes exactly the 10 START norm statements and keeps git; r=UNK removes both ASSIGN records. Residual failures: R-60-note, REGISTER-rule (k) and R-83 only. (This filter is itself post hoc.)
necessity_assessment.implicit_in_v1: v1 §1 already forbids non-act records, and outcome has an epistemic basis (SOURCE/DERIVED/UNKNOWN); a REFUSED coded from 'remains unauthorized' should be DERIVED. EVENTS.json carries no basis values, so whether v1 already discriminates is UNKNOWN, not 'no'.
necessity_assessment.fragility: k's demotion rests on 2 records: R-60-note (A: 'ambiguous', T2) and REGISTER-rule (GENERIC). If R-60-note is blind-recoded ACT-REFUSED, k becomes WEAK, not 0.

dual_nature_assessment.conclusion: Identified in §8 but not handled; the only repair mechanism (stated_by) is deferred.
dual_nature_assessment.prevalence: Every one of the 13 NORM records is the content of a ruling/annotation act (R-47, R-56, R-58, R-60, R-65, R-72, R-79, R-81, R-83, R-86, R-90). Several ACT outcomes rest on norm-type determinations: Chief's declined ADOPT (R-81 provenance annotation 'DOES NOT HOLD'), R-89 NOT-IN-FORCE (R-86 standing rule, per D2), R-91 held. Both surviving a-pairs, the only SUPPORTED core, sit on this boundary. F4 is not evaluated on the 36 although it could be now.
dual_nature_assessment.single_field_sufficient_for_act_only_cou: Only if observation_type is explicitly defined relative to the record's o ('is an attempt at or performance of o attested?'); the package never states this convention, so R-58-type rows remain coder-dependent.
dual_nature_assessment.single_field_insufficient_for_norm_datas: For norm records, a/r/s are ambiguous between the stating act and the governed act. The package flags only r; a is equally affected (START norms carry a=ENGINEERING but were stated by ARB/DA), so the NORM a=0 is an artefact.
dual_nature_assessment.recommended_two_level_form: Keep observation_type (defined relative to o) plus a mandatory, not deferred, source_act = {anchored row, operation that row itself performs}. NORM records' a/r/s describe the governed act; the stater is reached through source_act. NORM records never enter R3, so there is no double counting.

minimal_alternative.description: v1-internal rule change, no new field: (1) make the epistemic basis of outcome mandatory; (2) amend R3 so a record enters legality witnesses only if an attempt at or performance of o is attested by an anchored source (outcome basis SOURCE), excluding outcomes DERIVED from a permission statement; (3) anti-circularity clause: outcome may not be coded from the same text as the witnessed variable.
minimal_alternative.achieves: Act-only verdicts for k, s (via clause 3) and h; no records deleted.
minimal_alternative.costs: Norm records keep a misleading outcome value; the NORM dataset stays untyped; the dual-nature problem is not addressed.
minimal_alternative.relation_to_package: Smaller than the package's §4(a). The package's rejection of the outcome extension (§4c) partly rests on a false premise ('cannot express UNKNOWN'; under v1 §1 any unestablished field is already UNK); the overload objection stands.
